hypotheses.reasoning: enrichment-svc ran normally (POST /enrich ok, 25-90ms, heap healthy) until 16:54:39. From then on, its S3 PutObject calls to s3://ingest-artifacts-prod in us-east-1 started coming back as 500 InternalError and 503 ServiceUnavailable. These are fast server-side errors from AWS, not hangs. enrichment-svc then returns 500 'storage write failed' to ingest-api (#1325, #1693), which passes it on to ingest-gateway as POST /v1/events 500s (#1288 and later). The gateway's long latencies (19-29s) and the aws-sdk 'retry quota exhausted' warning (#1258) come from retries piling up on the failing S3 calls, not from a separate cause. I found no deploy lines. The status-poller timeouts to legacy-inventory, a deprecated endpoint, start at 16:41, before the S3 errors, and nothing on the request path depends on them, so I'm treating them as noise.
SDK retries amplified the S3 errors and made the gateway calls take much longer. But the trigger was the S3 errors themselves, not the retries.
status-poller healthchecks to legacy-inventory time out, but they start before the incident, the endpoint has been deprecated since 2025-06, and the failing request path doesn't use it.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the AWS Health Dashboard for an S3 problem in us-east-1. Meanwhile, make enrichment-svc's artifact upload non-blocking or best-effort (buffer to a local or durable queue and retry asynchronously), or temporarily switch writes to a bucket in another region, so /enrich doesn't fail when S3 does. Also lower SDK retry counts and timeouts so gateway latency stays down. Separately, remove the deprecated legacy-inventory healthcheck from status-poller.
